title.narrative: Activity under preparation Strengthening Ethnic Education - Myanmar ( SEE - Myanmar )

description.narrative: Myanmar is experiencing a protracted political, humanitarian and economic crisis, with widespread conflict, mass displacement, deepening poverty and recurrent natural disasters severely disrupting state education services and forcing large numbers of children and adolescents out of school or preventing them from enrolling. In many ethnic, rural and conflict¿affected areas, ethnic and community¿based providers act as de facto duty¿bearers, but their systems are fragmented, often lack formal recognition and face major institutional, financial and protection constraints. In this context, the action aims to strengthen local education systems and expand access to quality, inclusive education pathways in ethnic and conflict¿affected areas through three specific objectives: (i) strengthening ethnic and community¿based education systems and institutions, including coordination, governance, data and learner¿mobility frameworks (SO1); (ii) sustaining and expanding safe, inclusive and conflict¿sensitive education for displaced, out¿of¿school and other marginalised learners whose education has been interrupted, obstructed or ended by conflict (SO2); and (iii) enhancing learning quality, foundational skills and learner progression, particularly at secondary, TVET and post¿secondary levels, through recovery, bridging and skills¿oriented programmes linked to livelihoods (SO3). By delivering these results, the action is expected to make ethnic and community¿based systems more coherent, sustainable and protective, offering recognised, flexible pathways that enable crisis¿affected children and youth ¿ especially girls, displaced and at risk learners, and learners with disabilities to (re)enter and complete their education despite ongoing conflict and displacement, and to transition into decent work. Building on lessons from EU¿funded CASE2Learn and EASE programmes with the RISE Network, which expanded access to ethnic education and reduced out¿of¿school rates, the action is designed to tackle these conflict¿induced education gaps by expanding safe, flexible learning opportunities through ethnic and community¿based education providers and other non¿formal pathways that can reach displaced and conflict¿affected children and adolescents who are currently out of school. Moreover, the action shifts from access¿only support towards pathway development and system strengthening and aligns with the Joint Response Framework II[1] for coordinated education interventions after the 2021 coup. It contributes to the amended Regional MIP for Asia and the Pacific 2021¿2027 (section 1.3.4 ¿Priority area 4 ¿ Actions in countries in complex settings¿), supports the Education Pillar of the Team Europe Strategic Framework, and contributes primarily to SDG 16, while also advancing SDGs 1, 4, 5, 8 and 10. It is coded under DAC sectors 111 (Education), 112 (Basic education), 113 (Secondary education) and 114 (Post¿secondary education). The action is aligned with the EU Action Plan on Human Rights and Democracy, the EU¿s commitments on protecting children in armed conflict and the humanitarian¿development¿peace nexus. The action will contribute to the GAP III thematic of promoting women and girls¿ economic and social rights, as well as Specific Objective 1 of the country-level implementation plan (CLIP), ¿Increase resilience of women by supporting access to livelihoods and decent jobs¿.
